title: Sweetcorn and potato hash with eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Potatoes, corn on the cob, pepper, spring onions, eggs, cheddar and chives are all plain kitchen and garden foods.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket in August.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large lidded frying pan, a knife and a grater, and uses simple frying and baking eggs in hollows.

works.reason: 600g potatoes, two cobs and four eggs make a sensible hash for four, and the covered then uncovered frying and the 4 to 5 minutes for the eggs are realistic.

honest_times.reason: Twenty minutes of prep covers dicing the potatoes, cutting the kernels off the cobs and slicing the vegetables, and the 15, 8 and 5 minutes in the steps add up to the 28 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: 'Corn cobs' matches the sweetcorn id, and every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the chives and smoked paprika, is used in the steps.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fresh corn cut from the cob is at its peak in mid August, and it leads both the title and the hash.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English that a beginner can follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling breakfast of vegetables, potatoes, eggs and a little cheese that a family would happily eat again.
